latestRun.verification: GitHub/source review only; no Unity runtime or native capture was available. This run identified that major_light_leak was a hard automatic-fail defect with required human crop references but no current pixel-domain triage precondition comparable to obvious_repetition. Added warning-only bright-on-dark diagnostics over five canonical 100% crops. A sampled pixel qualifies only when it is bright, strongly exceeds a dark surrounding annulus, and most annulus samples remain dark; candidates are then clustered into 32 px blocks to de-emphasize isolated sparkle. The runtime report binds the current 4K manifest SHA-256 and each crop SHA-256 and cannot award points, clear the defect or assert it automatically. Native4KReviewPacket now validates the contract before preparation and generates the report after sealed still/temporal evidence. Reviewed-evidence integrity schema 1.2 requires a current light-leak report before the core Visual Fidelity evaluator can score. During editing, an accidental source typo was introduced in an intermediate reviewed-evidence-validator commit and corrected immediately in b8fc5b7; the final source was re-fetched around the affected region and is syntactically restored there. No Unity compile/runtime assertions are made.
expectedVisualScoreImpact: Critical major light leak: improves the probability that spatially persistent bright seams/holes in final post-tonemap pixels are surfaced before scoring; it does not automatically fail or clear the defect.
Lighting/shadows/reflections: prioritizes inspection of anomalous bright-on-dark discontinuities that source-only sun/shadow coherence cannot prove absent.
Geometry & construction: helps direct actual-pixel review toward possible shell/aperture/interface closure defects rather than treating source geometry QA as sufficient.
Cinematic image: uses the final display-transformed pixels, so exposure/tonemap-induced false positives remain visible to the reviewer instead of being hidden by source assumptions.
